column3: NASB’s “What, therefore, belongs to the Levites may be redeemed” interprets a difficult clause, “and whoever redeems from the Levites”; the meaning is uncertain.
“his means … falter” renders “his hand slips”; NASB adds “like” to “a stranger or a sojourner,” and the sense is uncertain.
“usurious interest” renders two terms, “interest and increase,” and “revere” renders “fear.”
“his family” renders “his clan,” and “his forefathers” renders “his fathers.”
“use them as permanent slaves” renders “work with them forever.”
“the means … becomes sufficient” renders “the hand … reaches.”
“his blood relatives” renders “the kin of his flesh,” and “if he prospers” renders “if his hand reaches.”
“in proportion to them” renders “according to their mouth.”
